title: every-probe-has-a-receiver
intention: Every standing probe-bearing WATCHME spec names a receiver that actually uses its data, in a component, and has that receiver built; a WATCHME for which no receiver could really use the data is a design fault and its ticket goes to FIXME — no receiver is invented to justify a probe.
why: A probe that fires with nobody using its data is spend with no return and a watch that looks armed while nothing acts on it: 138 standing probe specs, 0 receivers (measured 2026-10-01). Akien: 'for all watchmes that we built probes for but not recievers, i think we just build the recievers?'
traces_to: Akien's ruling 2026-09-30 a-probe-needs-a-consumer ('no consumer that USES the data = trash; receiver first'); Law 1 (a probe nobody reads is spend with no return); Law 9 (the 138 are red until each is measured); RULE 1 (each receiver build is inside its component).
how: Measured 2026-10-01 over CairnCommons/tickets: 138 probe-bearing WATCHME specs, 0 carry a receiver; 88 name a probe file that exists, 50 do not; 112 sit on PROVED tickets. Grouped by the probe's component: cairn/tools/base 22, inference_domain 11, tester 9, build_inspector 8, ground_loop 8, librarian 5, then ~40 components with 1-4 each. Per probe, read the standing WATCHME (object, trigger, enough, carrier, nexus, consumer) and the probe's code, then ONE of: (a) a receiver in some component would really use the data -> build it (receiver first, firing on the probe's event, crossing components only over the bus per RULE 1) and write the receiver {what, in} into the spec through the artifact door; (b) the probe file is gone but moved -> repoint the spec's probe, then (a) or (c); (c) no receiver could use it -> the ticket goes to FIXME with the lack named. One child per component (RULE 1: a build and its proofs stay inside the component), the largest first.
falsifier: GREEN when a census over CairnCommons/tickets finds zero probe-bearing WATCHME specs that lack a receiver dict on a ticket not standing at FIXME, and every child is PROVED. RED if any such spec remains at the horizon, or if a receiver was added whose 'in' component has no code that reads the probe's carrier (a receiver written to satisfy the field). WRONG INTENT if a probe's data has a plausible reader that only Akien's judgment can name — one question on that child, with the measurement. Horizon: the last child PROVED.
watchme: none, because the standing measurement is the ticket inspector's watchme_present check, which reports watchme_spec_error (receiver required) on every ticket at every pass once de9e31ef104c lands; a probe spec without a receiver reds there, so a watch would learn nothing new
children: probe-paths-that-name-nothing — the 50 specs whose probe file does not exist: read each, repoint a moved probe, or send its ticket to FIXME (a WATCHME whose probe was never built is incomplete). Runs FIRST: it shrinks every per-component child, and measures whether PROVED -> FIXME is a legal back-edge.

the-remaining-components-probes-get-receivers — every other component (librarian 5; cairn device, operator_inbox 4 each; aider_shim, learning_block, rehearsal, codemother, corrosion, db_domain, cc 3 each; then 1-2 each), cast one child per component as it is reached, from this parent.
gates_bound: concept-piece prove_gate: CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-every-probe-has-a-receiver.md carrying Akien's W2 words verbatim and the per-probe disposition rule, sealed by quorum.seal; PROVEME additionally requires every child PROVED and the census at zero. Durability: committed and pushed in both repos.
builder_notes: A Haiku builder would ask: (1) How do I find a component's probes? the census script in the parent's how: every ticket whose watchme (dict or list) has a 'probe', grouped by the innermost intention+why.json dir above the probe path. (2) What counts as 'really uses'? code in the receiver's component that reads the probe's carrier and changes a decision or a record on it — logging it is not use. (3) What if unsure? read the spec's consumer and the ticket's why; if still undecidable, one question on that child with the measurement.

decisions.text: MEASURED 2026-10-01 (find over the repo for each missing probe basename): of 50 — (1) 5 sit on KILLED/SUPERSEDED tickets: terminal, out of the census, no action; (2) 22 sit on tickets not yet built (TICKETME/BUILDME/WATCHME waiting): the probe is unbuilt because the ticket is, and their spec gains a receiver before their own BUILDME (the gate now refuses a spec without one), not here; (3) 13 were MOVED — 7 builder/machines/* -> codemother/machines/*, 4 harbor_master -> cairn/machines/harbor_master, 1 tools/base -> tools/bus_client, (and 0cde/2b16/faa5 harbor_master) — repoint the spec, then dispose as any standing probe; (4) 5 aider_shim probes sit in probes_disabled/ on PROVED tickets: disabled, so no firing and no receiver — their WATCHME goes to FIXME unless the aider shim re-enables them; (5) the rest, PROVED with no file anywhere (7 ground_loop: 0d16e513ff26, 2f0a6ea8c966, 7ecdce95c42c, 82725b223559, a66af26de84d, b5b5e0483af1, ffc775a09d54; tester 712bac150b3f): read the ticket and the git log for the deletion; a probe deleted by a ruling (ground-loop-is-just-the-heartbeat) is a WATCHME retired by design -> FIXME with the ruling named. Also MEASURED: PROVED -> FIXME is a legal back-edge — emit('code-seam@v2: ... -> [PROVED]', 'FIXME', missing=[...]) returns '... TICKETME -> [FIXME:waiting] -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> PROVED'.
decisions.step: unlisted: classify the 50 specs whose probe file does not exist

decisions.text: MEASURED 2026-10-03, census over CairnCommons/tickets: 129 probe-bearing WATCHME specs, 0 with a receiver. 8 are SUPERSEDED and 2 KILLED (terminal). 4 are at FIXME. 23 sit on unbuilt tickets (TICKETME/BUILDME), which get their receiver at their own BUILDME. 90 are standing (81 PROVED, 9 WATCHME) and their probe files load; 2 more WATCHME specs name a missing file. The 90 standing PROBEs post to: harbor_master 73, tester 6, codemother 4, inference_domain 3, cairn 1, cairnmap 1, charter 1, press_office 1. None sets a verb. Every one of their whys asks whether its ticket's intention still holds under live use, which is the WATCHME's own question (the /sorted default carrier is 'a verdict against THIS ticket's falsifier'). Nothing reads any of it: verbless mail falls to BaseDevice.receive, which only emits 'received' (cairn/tools/base/device.py:260-280; RECORDER_ON_READ is set by no device). DESIGN: the one component that uses a WATCHME verdict is the one that moves ticket state, harbor_master. A red finding is design work the ticket owns (72d2f79daf0a, 973574dddb77), and clearance._send_to_fixme (cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master/clearance.py:1025) already performs that back-edge through the artifact door. So: child 1 builds a harbor_master bus verb 'watch' whose body is {ticket, holds: bool, finding}. holds False sends the ticket to FIXME with the finding as its one lack. holds True changes nothing and says so in the reply. The receiver is built first. The remaining children, one per component that holds standing probes, give each PROBE verb='watch', to='harbor_master', and a carry returning {ticket, holds, finding}, and write receiver {what: 'harbor_master watch verb', in: 'cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master'} into each spec through the artifact door. A probe whose data cannot be stated as holds/finding against its own ticket's falsifier has no receiver, and its ticket goes to FIXME (case c), with nothing invented. Firing the probes on their events once 164da559823d cuts the beat is NOT this ticket's work.
